name: gardner with spies
description: Martin Gardner's 5x5 minichess with each side's c-pawn replaced by a spy, a piece that steps one square straight in any direction and can never capture. There is no check: the king is simply captured, and the side that loses its king loses. While both spies stand, players take turns as usual. When a spy is taken, its owner first plays one ordinary reply move if it is their turn, so the spy's taker can be recaptured; from then on both players move at once in rounds, and the player without a spy must choose first and show their move to the other, who chooses knowing it, before both moves are made together. Once both spies are gone, both choose in secret. In a round only two pieces moving onto the same square collide: two of the ordinary pieces are both removed, and a spy is always the one removed. A piece that moves onto a square its target has just left lands there if it could move to an empty square, so two pieces that try to take each other in the same round trade places unharmed; a pawn's diagonal capture, which cannot land on an empty square, misses and the pawn stays. Two such misses at each other two rounds in a row bar that pair of captures until either square changes. If both kings fall in the same round the game is drawn. A round counts as two moves on the clocks. The spy is worth what it lets its owner see: the side that keeps it answers every move with the move already in view, so it can step any attacked piece out of the way and take whatever the other side leaves standing.

provenance.preview: A preview: a new kind of game in which a lost spy turns the game into rounds, still being tested. Play it against the computer for practice; it is on no leaderboard yet, and its score is a first reading, not yet trusted.
